transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to sit still. It's like... I don't know, like I've got this motor humming under my skin. Especially when I'm supposed to be sitting quietly, you know? Like during staff meetings at work, or... or briefings for church events. I just end up shifting around in my seat, or I have to stand up, or I just find some excuse to get up and move. It's... yeah, that's about it.
When you’re sitting still, do you feel an inner urge or pressure to move?
Yeah... like I just said, it's that motor feeling. It's just this pressure where I need to get up and do something else.
Did this restless feeling start after you began taking a psychiatric medication or after the dose was increased?
No. I don't... I haven't taken any medications like that.
Did you have this same trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah... I suppose so. I remember getting in trouble a lot back in grade school. Just... popping out of my seat. Or talking over the teacher, rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. My mother... she used to say I acted like I was wound too tight. So, yeah. Even as a kid.
Do you ever have sudden movements or sounds that happen on their own and are hard to control?
No. I don't... nothing like that. I don't make noises or anything. Just what we already talked about.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on tasks?
No, not really. I mean... I do my job just fine. I get things done. I just... I don't think I have a problem with that.
Do you often talk more than other people or blurt things out before others are finished speaking?

Yeah, I suppose. Sometimes. Like... if my supervisor is giving me instructions, or one of the staff over at the church. I just... I tend to jump in before they finish. I think I know what they're going to say, so I just say it. But then sometimes I get it wrong, and... they have to correct me. So, yeah. I guess I do that.
Have these restlessness and interrupting habits caused problems for you at work, at church, or in other parts of your life?

Yeah... I suppose. Mostly at work. There have been some complaints, I guess. Because I miss parts of the instructions, they have to correct me a lot. It just... it creates some friction. Especially during room turnovers, or when we're figuring out the supply decisions. It actually got to the point where... well, my supervisor kind of pushed me toward the employee assistance program. So... yeah.
